description:
## Goal

Make runtime-demand derivation schedule-order independent before moving it onto
the reactive scheduler.

settle_demand_cone currently sorts members by StableSortKey because deriving
callable-flow facts mints fresh Ty combinations as a side effect. Its comment
states that HashMap iteration order otherwise changes type-interning order and
downstream identities. A reactive worklist intentionally evaluates only changed
formulas and therefore cannot preserve a global member order.

## Repro (measured 2026-08-26, release, 00420_enum_take_drop_split)

Method: at the end of a compile, dump `(id, Types::display(Ty(id)))` for every
interner arena slot; run in four SEPARATE PROCESSES and diff.

Result: four different arenas, identical length (1,424 slots), exactly 16
differing lines in four clusters:

    a1_v0 <-> a1_v1, a4_v0 <-> a4_v1, a4_u0_1_v0 <-> a4_u0_1_v1   address vars
    {:cont,A}|{:cont,B} <-> A|B                                   (two clusters)
    ids 1006-1009                                                 NOT this ticket

THIS ticket owns the first three: genuinely different types whose MINT ORDER
depends on upstream iteration order.

The interner itself is not at fault. `TypeInterner::intern` (`types/mod.rs:125`)
dedupes on `Descr` equality and assigns `Ty(arena.len())` -- a pure function of
its call SEQUENCE. So a differing arena proves the call SEQUENCE differs, which
is exactly this ticket's subject.

The fourth cluster is an interner canonicalization gap (two slots holding
equivalent types) and is fz-kdt.48, not this.

### Sharpest lead

`Types.address_vars` is documented as "keyed by the address path so the same
address always yields the same TypeVarId, making the addressed arrow canonical by
construction" (`types/mod.rs`) -- yet `a4_v1` is minted BEFORE `a4_v0` in some
runs. Whatever iterates the variable set before minting is an order-dependent
site. Start there.

### Boundary: no work divergence is observed

Across those same runs, program output and the entire public work SEQUENCE (event
name + kind + job kind, 17,574 events) are byte-identical. The renumbering does
not currently flip observable work. It does feed two production sorts
(fz-kdt.49), and the current log cannot distinguish identical work from an
identical kind-sequence with permuted identities until fz-kdt.34 lands. So treat
"no divergence" as measured-so-far, not proven.

### Do not expect fz-f98.21 to cover this

f98.21's canonical external form deliberately makes this defect INVISIBLE, because
every position renders the same. That is by design: canonical form measures the
artifact, this ticket measures the cause. Neither replaces the other.

## Output contract

- Deriving one executable's runtime demand is a pure function of authoritative
  facts and current demand inputs, modulo semantic type interning.
- Evaluating independent demand formulas in different orders produces
  semantically and externally identical facts and byte-identical backend programs.
- No demand formula depends on a prior formula having minted a raw Ty id first.
- Determinism comes from canonical data, not a sorting barrier or scheduler order.

## TDD strategy

1. Add a focused harness that evaluates the same independent/cyclic demand
   formulas in several explicit orders and compares canonical demand/callable-flow
   facts plus backend output.
2. Adopt the arena-dump repro above as a regression test: N separate processes,
   identical arenas.
3. Instrument type creation in derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable_product,
   ground_dispatch_surfaces, callable boundary contributions, and related
   own_surface/boundary-demand paths.
4. Move type construction to the earliest authoritative fact, reuse an existing
   canonical type, or make the interning key structurally canonical.
5. Delete the StableSortKey ordering dependency and its explanatory workaround
   once the shuffled-order test is green.

Do not add another sort, stable-id translation table, or demand-local type cache.

## Telemetry acceptance

Consumes fz-kdt.34.

- order-shuffled runs publish the same semantic facts and causal work multiset;
- raw scheduler order may differ without changing output;
- no type-mint event is attributable solely to which independent demand formula
  ran first.

## Checks

- Focused order-shuffle test.
- The four-process arena-identity test above.
- Existing byte-identical backend-program determinism tests.
- Both target fixtures across interp, run, and build.
- Full lib and single-threaded fixture matrix.
- Documentation removes the claim that demand settlement requires a stable global
  member order.
title: Make runtime-demand derivation order-independent before reactive scheduling
